title: Carnivals and circuses with Doc Cheatham
summary: The group played circuses and carnivals, which she hated, with Doc Cheatham, Briscoe and guitarist Joe Williams, scraping by on little money.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How long did this go on, a couple years?

During this period we played for circuses and carnivals and that is the worst life that anybody could ever - oh, my goodness. I thought about that and I just shivered in bed once because these roustabouts - you call them that? - they are terrible... Doc Cheatham, good trumpeter, did you ever hear of him? He sounded like an [ ]. He was sensational. He was with us during that period and we played some really rough places. That's a terrible life.
When you worked a carnival what did you do for a piano?
Oh, they had a piano, there was always a piano there.
Did the carnival provide it or did you have to carry it with you?
I really don't know. No, we didn't have enough money to carry anything with us. We were just barely making it.
Speaking of Doc Cheatham, who else was in your group?

Doc Cheatham, Briscoe, and Joe Williams, a terrific guitarist. He made a banjo sound like a guitar and I loved it, because banjos - I used to hate the sound of them. He was very good. Briscoe and a drummer - I have forgotten his name completely. Later on with Seymour and Jeanette
